description: Compiles SIZE/4 distinct generated regexes and as many repeated ones, then runs one log-line regex with numbered and named captures, test(), a lastIndex-driven global loop, match/matchAll and replace with callbacks and substitution patterns.
notes: Generated patterns avoid '/' and line terminators, and only re.source.length is hashed, because the exact escaping of `source` is partly implementation-defined. Alternations stay well under 64 alternatives.

description: Runs u-flag property-escape, lookbehind and split regexes over mixed-script sentences, fixed case-folding probes, and tokenizes a generated program of SIZE statements with a sticky combined regex and with a list of sticky regexes.

Builds a SIZE-record ASCII string by += and by join, then slices and searches it at random offsets, splits/joins/replaces its lines, runs short-string padding/trim/case operations and reads it at random indices.
notes: Full-string scans for absent needles are a fixed 8 rounds so that the run stays linear in SIZE. The large size is 6x the medium one: at 8x, random reads into the 17 MB string became cache-bound on every engine (the random-read section grew 16x on qjs), and the run reached 6.5 s on ZIPP.

covers: toUpperCase / toLowerCase on non-ASCII (special casing, final sigma)

description: Walks and rebuilds a 4*SIZE-code-point mixed-script string, iterates it by code point, case-maps and normalizes non-ASCII words, searches a large well-formed two-byte string, and round-trips text through the URI coders.
notes: Three ZIPP slow paths found while writing this (all outputs identical, so none is a correctness bug). (1) Array.prototype.slice(i, i + 16) costs O(array length) per call in both the interpreter and the JIT tier. The likely cause is that the dense path of the "slice" arm in crates/zipp-vm/src/vm/array_ops.rs calls array_has_holes, which scans the whole array, where scanning items[start..end] would do. The chunks are therefore copied into a scratch array, since slicing a 4*SIZE array made this section quadratic (6 s of 9.7 s at the large size). (2) indexOf/lastIndexOf on a string that holds a lone surrogate is O(length) per call: a find-all loop over 48K units took 112 ms, against 0 ms for the same slice+concat construction when it stays well formed. `big` is cut on code-point boundaries so it stays well formed. (3) UTF-16 index access into non-ASCII strings is O(distance from the last position) (WTF-8 storage with a one-position memo): the random-start searches run on a 16,000-unit document so that their cost does not grow with SIZE. That share is left in the workload on purpose, and it is most of ZIPP's deficit here.

covers: string escaping: quotes, backslash, control characters
description: Round-trips SIZE varied API-message objects through JSON.stringify and JSON.parse, with a reviver, function and array replacers, indentation, nested arrays and escaped strings.

WeakMap get/set/has/delete with object, array and function keys
description: Churns Map and Set with mixed-type keys at ~8, ~1k and ~SIZE live entries, iterates them, deletes 90% of a SIZE/2 map and walks it while mutating, and exercises a WeakMap of SIZE/4 object keys.
notes: The large tier scales with SIZE (about 110k live keys at the medium size, about 1.1k at the small size) so that the small run stays about 1/100 of the medium work; the ~8 and ~1k tiers are fixed.

description: Formats and parses SIZE integers and doubles through toString(radix), toFixed/toPrecision/toExponential, String() and parseInt/parseFloat/Number(), runs exact and quantised Math functions, and does 64-256-bit BigInt arithmetic with toString.
notes: Implementation-approximated Math results (pow, exp, log, sin, cos, tanh, atan2, hypot, cbrt) are quantised before hashing; numeric strings are kept at 20 significant digits or fewer so that parsing is exactly specified.
